claim: Proxmox states containers share the host kernel and that full VMs provide better isolation; unprivileged containers map container root to an unprivileged host UID; FUSE inside containers is strongly discouraged because containers must be frozen for snapshot backups.
quote: Containers use the kernel of the host system. This exposes an attack surface for malicious users. In general, full virtual machines provide better isolation.

claim: LXC upstream's official position is that privileged containers cannot be root-safe, while unprivileged containers are safe by design because container uid 0 maps to an unprivileged host user.
quote: LXC upstream's position is that those containers aren't and cannot be root-safe.

claim: Anthropic recommends a dedicated VM for untrusted repositories, describing it as the strongest separation with its own kernel and kernel-level separation between agent and host.
quote: A dedicated virtual machine provides the strongest separation, with its own kernel and, in cloud or microVM deployments, its own virtualized hardware.

claim: The Proxmox firewall runs host-side as an iptables service per node, has cluster/host/guest levels with config files, must be enabled both at datacenter level and per network device, and supports security groups and IP sets.
quote: Each virtual network device has its own firewall enable flag.

claim: ZFS and LVM-thin do native block-level snapshots; internal qcow2 snapshots on directory/NFS/CIFS block a running VM and can take minutes to hours on large disks.
quote: Creating and deleting internal qcow2 snapshots will block a running VM and is not an efficient operation.

claim: Proxmox forum consensus and staff position is that Docker inside LXC is unsupported and may break, and that QEMU/KVM VMs should be used for Docker for best isolation.
quote: Don't use docker inside an lxc, this isn't really supported and might break at any time

claim: Proxmox's container chapter recommends nesting containers inside a QEMU VM for maximum isolation, repeats the LXC team's 'unsafe' verdict on privileged containers, and warns never to bind mount system directories into a container.
quote: Never bind mount system directories like /, /var or /etc into a container - this poses a great security risk.

claim: Docker does not work in unprivileged LXC on current Proxmox kernels (runc sysctl write needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, AppArmor profile probe is host-root-owned); the privileged workaround requires nesting/keyctl/fuse plus unconfined AppArmor and is a performance choice, not a security choice. VM overhead cited as ~200 MB plus a 2-second boot delay.
quote: Stop trying to make unprivileged Docker work on recent Proxmox kernels

claim: Proxmox staff acknowledge that breaking out of an LXC remains possible when nesting is enabled, and recommend a VM for untrusted workloads because VMs have fully virtualized kernels.
quote: it can still be possible to break out of the LXC when nesting is enabled, but as you mentioned the uid of the LXC-root is an unprivileged user on the PVE host.

claim: Practitioners sandboxing coding agents range from fully airgapped separate systems to dockerized git worktrees, with widespread dissatisfaction about friction.
quote: Currently I'm using docker-ized git worktrees so I can dangerously skip permissions. It's not great.

claim: A 2026 HN survey of AI coding agent sandboxing finds the field split mainly between containers and minimal/no isolation, with a minority using KVM/QEMU VMs and SSH-based interaction with dedicated unprivileged accounts.
quote: give an agent its own unprivileged user account and interact with it via sudo, SSH, and shared directories

claim: Sandbox-infrastructure comparison for 2026: standard containers are insufficient for untrusted code because they share the host kernel; Firecracker microVMs boot in ~125 ms with under 5 MiB overhead per VM and give hardware-enforced isolation.
quote: less than 5 MiB overhead per VM

claim: Academic work in 2026 quantifies frontier LLM capability at escaping container sandboxes, evaluating identification and exploitation of container misconfigurations.
quote: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape

claim: The June 2026 Mastra npm compromise poisoned 140+ packages with a dayjs typosquat whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper that disabled TLS verification and harvested developer credentials and tokens.
quote: Over 140 packages across the mastra and @mastra scopes were compromised through account takeover

claim: Proxmox VE minimum and recommended requirements: 1 GB RAM minimum, recommended 2 GB for the OS and PVE services plus memory designated for guests, and roughly 1 GB memory per TB of used storage for ZFS/Ceph.
quote: Minimum 2 GB for the OS and Proxmox VE services, plus designated memory for guests.

claim: On PVE 8.1+ installs the ZFS ARC limit defaults to 10% of host memory clamped to 16 GiB; the sizing rule is 2 GiB base plus 1 GiB per TiB of pool; older installs may be uncapped at 50%+ and should be limited via zfs_arc_max in /etc/modprobe.d/zfs.conf.
quote: 10 % of the host memory, clamped to a maximum of 16 GiB

claim: Proxmox VM tuning: setting min memory equal to max allocates directly instead of ballooning; ballooning under host pressure can trigger guest swap or the OOM killer; cpulimit caps total host CPU time as a fraction; VirtIO SCSI single with IO thread is current best practice; discard shrinks thin-provisioned images.
quote: VirtIO SCSI single with IO Thread enabled represents current best practice

claim: VS Code Server runs on the remote machine as the user you signed in with, requires kernel >= 4.18 and glibc >= 2.28, and workspace extensions get full access to the source code, remote filesystem and remote APIs.
quote: Workspace extensions run in a remote extension host with the workspace and have full access to the source code, remote filesystem, and remote APIs.

claim: code tunnel connects without SSH by making outbound connections to a Microsoft service hosted in Azure and requires the same GitHub or Microsoft account on both ends.
quote: VS Code will make outbound connections to a service hosted in Azure; no firewall changes are generally necessary

claim: JetBrains remote-development guidance for larger projects is to add CPUs and RAM, enable swap, and use local SSD storage; single-board computers and shared hosting are unsupported.
quote: Enabling Swap is recommended. Even on cloud instances

claim: Mosh survives roaming between networks and laptop sleep, provides local echo, runs over UDP ports 60000-61000, and authenticates by logging in over SSH first.
quote: logs in to the server via SSH, and users present the same credentials (e.g., password, public key) as before

claim: A February 2026 practitioner write-up drives Claude Code remotely with mosh for connection resilience, tmux for session persistence with auto-attach on login, and Claude Code hooks pushing ntfy notifications on questions, completion and errors.
quote: mosh handles the flaky mobile connection (WiFi to cellular transitions, dead zones, phone sleeping), while tmux handles session persistence

claim: claude -p/--print runs the agent loop non-interactively; --output-format json returns result, session_id and total_cost_usd; --bare skips discovery of hooks, plugins, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md for reproducible scripted runs; --allowedTools pre-approves tools and --resume continues a session.
quote: Add --bare to reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md.

claim: qm snapshot takes an optional --vmstate to save RAM; qm rollback does not start the VM unless --start is passed, and VMs auto-start when the snapshot includes RAM; qm guest exec and exec-status run commands via the guest agent; qm clone and qm template manage templates.
quote: Whether the VM should get started after rolling back successfully. (Note: VMs will be automatically started if the snapshot includes RAM.)

claim: Containers use the same snapshot verbs as VMs (pct snapshot / rollback --start / listsnapshot / delsnapshot) and pct exec / pct enter run commands or a shell inside a container from the host.
quote: Rollback LXC state to specified snapshot.

claim: virtiofs in Proxmox 8.4+ is configured via Datacenter > Directory Mappings plus a VirtioFS hardware device and mounted with mount -t virtiofs TAG; it exposes host filesystem permissions directly, blocks live migration, and community testing finds it significantly slower than NFS.
quote: can't live migrate running VM which uses following mapped devices: virtiofs0

claim: Benchmarks of NFS vs SMB vs SSHFS: NFS dominates small random 4K operations and is fastest in plaintext; SSHFS is the fastest encrypted option and more CPU-efficient, only slightly slower than plaintext NFS.
quote: NFS without encryption is the best choice on Linux for maximum performance. If you want encryption i would recommend SSHFS

claim: Snapshots without RAM roll back as if the guest had suffered a power outage; snapshots with RAM write a vmstate volume the size of guest memory (observed ~21 GB per snapshot) regardless of disk changes.
quote: if you snapshot without dumping the RAM and you will do a rollback, it will be as if the LXC/VM encountered a power outage and crashed

claim: The QEMU guest agent is enabled with qm set VMID --agent 1 and, when running in the guest, calls guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw around backups and snapshots to improve consistency.
quote: calls guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw to improve consistency

claim: A Proxmox Linux bridge is a virtual switch; setting bridge-vlan-aware yes makes it VLAN-aware so a per-guest VLAN tag works transparently; a bridge with bridge-ports none has no physical uplink and creates an isolated guest network or a NAT/masquerade setup.
quote: It can be thought of as a virtual switch which the guests and physical interfaces are connected to.

claim: A Proxmox SDN Simple zone creates an isolated VNet bridge that is not linked to a physical interface, with traffic local to each node, and can be used in NAT or routed setups.
quote: is not linked to a physical interface, and VM traffic is only local on each the node

claim: Proxmox forum finding that SDN Simple zones do not actually isolate guests by default because they lack a dedicated VRF, and that real isolation requires layering Proxmox firewall rules at datacenter/node/VM/NIC level (accept intra-subnet, accept gateway, drop cross-subnet).
quote: currently simple zones don't use dedicated vrf

claim: Recipe for isolated topologies in Proxmox using SDN VNets plus an OPNsense router VM: assign a NIC per VNet, set static gateway IPs per interface, serve DHCP/DNS with Dnsmasq, and control traffic with interface-based firewall rules.
quote: Ensure you provide a DNS Server so VMs can resolve web addresses

claim: Trusted X11 forwarding lets a malicious remote capture keystrokes and mouse events, inspect or manipulate other windows, read and write the clipboard, and take screenshots; ssh -X is restricted by the X11 SECURITY extension and ForwardX11Trusted no should be set explicitly.
quote: Capture keystrokes and mouse events; Inspect or manipulate other application windows; Read from or write to the clipboard and selections.

claim: Anyone with root on a remote host can use a forwarded SSH agent socket to authenticate as you to other systems without ever touching your private key files.
quote: anyone with root access on the remote host can discreetly access your local SSH agent through the socket

claim: A GitHub deploy key is an SSH key granting access to a single repository, read-only by default, with the private half staying on the server; its documented drawbacks are no passphrase and no expiry, and agent forwarding cannot be used for automated deploys.
quote: an SSH key that grants access to a single repository. GitHub attaches the public part of the key directly to your repository instead of a personal account, and the private part of the key remains on your server.

claim: Concrete qm command sequence for building a cloud-init template (qm create, importdisk, --ide2 cloudinit, --ciuser/--sshkey/--ipconfig0, qm template) and cloning it to a working VM.
quote: qm clone 9000 101 --name ubuntu-node1 --full

claim: Proxmox VE 9.2 was released 21 May 2026 on Debian 13.5 with Linux kernel 7.0, QEMU 11.0, LXC 7.0 and ZFS 2.4, and expanded the SDN stack with WireGuard and BGP fabric protocols.
quote: Native support for WireGuard and BGP has been integrated into the SDN stack

claim: Claude Code's sandbox docs state sandboxing is not a complete isolation boundary, warn that broad domain allowlists enable exfiltration because the proxy does not inspect TLS, note that exposing docker.sock effectively grants host access, flag writable $PATH/shell-config directories as escalation paths, and record that --dangerously-skip-permissions is blocked when running as root.
quote: Sandboxing reduces risk but is not a complete isolation boundary.

claim: A practitioner runs per-language Proxmox LXC dev environments accessed with the VS Code Remote-SSH extension, describing the benefit as dependency isolation rather than security, and suited to web/console apps.
quote: Each project and language resides in its own container, preventing dependency conflicts and ensuring a clean development space.

claim: Proxmox forum framing of LXC as a semi-isolated environment that can leak or interfere with the host under extreme conditions because containers run directly on it, versus VMs for isolation.
quote: They can leak or interfere with the host under extreme conditions because they run directly on the host

claim: Measured tsc heap usage scales with type surface rather than project size: 61 MB on an empty project versus 465 MB with aws-sdk types in scope, and large real projects run close to the Node memory limit and frequently go out of memory.
quote: was running very close to the node memory limit, and would frequently just go out of memory
